points.name: health.stress.settings.monitor_register
points.interpretation: The page builder registers callback 0x0c633885 with event filter 7 and user data 0.

points.name: health.stress.settings.relax_register
points.interpretation: The page builder registers callback 0x0c63373d with event filter 7 and user data 0.

points.name: health.stress.settings.relax_initial_hide
points.interpretation: When the monitor status is not 1 the builder adds flag 1 to the reminder row.

points.name: health.stress.settings.relax_initial_show
points.interpretation: When the monitor status is 1 the builder clears flag 1 on the reminder row.

points.name: health.stress.settings.relax_monitor_hide
points.interpretation: The monitor callback adds flag 1 to the reminder row on its state-change path.

points.name: health.stress.settings.relax_refresh_hide
points.interpretation: The settings event listener adds flag 1 to the reminder row when the monitor status is not 1.

points.name: health.stress.settings.relax_refresh_show
points.interpretation: The settings event listener clears flag 1 on the reminder row when the monitor status is 1.

evidence: The pressure application registers the settings page descriptor. Its create stores the root and invokes the builder. The builder registers two event filter 7 callbacks for monitor and relax reminder rows. The monitor callback updates monitoring state and can hide the reminder row; the relax callback updates setting state. A settings event listener refreshes row visibility and switch state. Destroy clears the root.
scope: Only recorded switch registrations and row visibility calls while the pressure settings root is active. Other ways of changing monitoring, persisted settings, and notification delivery are not intercepted.
limitations: Replacing callbacks or hiding the row may desynchronize displayed and actual settings. Root slots are not thread barriers; shared-entry publication and rollback require system-wide quiescence. Device behavior remains unverified.
